status.label: Needs environment details after non-repro
status.detail: The reporter gives a plausible FancyZones regression, but a collaborator already commented that they cannot reproduce it on a newer build and the issue still lacks a bug-report ZIP, zone layout, monitor setup, or video.

next_action.label: Request a focused FancyZones repro package
next_action.reason: Need the exact zone layout, monitor configuration, app/window type, and a fresh bug-report ZIP to determine whether this is a real FancyZones regression or a local window-management interaction.

actions.label: Ask for layout, monitor, and repro evidence

comment.body: Thanks for the report. We could not reproduce this yet on a newer build, so could you retest on the latest PowerToys release and attach a fresh Report Bug ZIP? Please also include your monitor count/resolutions, the FancyZones layout in use, which app window you double-click, whether the window was placed with FancyZones or Windows Snap immediately beforehand, and a short recording showing the height-maximize turning into full maximize.

actions.note: Draft only; no upstream comment is posted without explicit approval.

judgment.rationale: The report is specific enough to be believable, but the single live maintainer signal is a non-repro on a newer build and the issue does not yet contain the configuration details needed to isolate why FancyZones behaves differently from Windows Snap.
evidence: The issue says only FancyZones-placed windows maximize to the whole screen when the top edge is double-clicked, while Windows Snap still behaves correctly.
Collaborator jiripolasek commented on 2026-08-13 that they could not reproduce the problem on PT v0.101.2222 / Windows 11 28120.2630.
There is no attached Report Bug ZIP, linked PR, assignee, monitor layout description, or video showing the exact zone placement before the failure.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask for a fresh bug report, exact zone/monitor setup, and a short recording before scheduling engineering work.
